findings.text: The change divides keyed busy time by min(window, now - first admission) rather than the window length, but section 21's change 2 and its definitions still define requests_per_run as the busy request-seconds divided by the window length and name only two null conditions for the derived figures (fewer than three live runs, or under 300 s of router history). The code now carries a third regime (300 s <= observed < 900 s) whose published ratio and worker_slots differ from the plan's literal formula; on the plan's own acceptance fixture (14 runs, 5,940 busy seconds 'over a 900 s window') the plan's literal rule gives 0.471 and the node's rule gives 0.707 unless the fixture's admissions open a full window before the snapshot, which the node moved them to do (tests/test_agent_router_worker_slots.py:33 now admits at now-900, not now-600). The behaviour is the correct mean-simultaneous-requests-per-run and is exactly what the workstation dispatch rule anticipates ('unless the admission block also publishes observed_seconds'), so nothing under imas_ambix/ is wrong; what is missing is the plan text, which should name the observed-span divisor, carry observed_seconds, and fix that regime's precedence.

observed_seconds is published beside window_seconds, but no test asserts it when the router has observed the full window: the fleet fixture asserts window_seconds == 900 and the ratio 0.471, never observed_seconds, so the min(window, ...) cap is pinned only from below (the 320 s and 600 s cases). A cap removed or raised would still pass the head gate because every fixture sits at or below the window.

follow_ons: section 21's definitions should carry the observed-span divisor and the observed_seconds field, and state the precedence of the 300 s-<900 s regime over both the plan's literal full-window divisor and the congested clamp; until then the code and the plan text disagree on what requests_per_run means for a router younger than its window.
the observed_seconds cap at the window is unpinned in the suite (no fixture runs with first admission 900 s or more before the snapshot and asserts observed_seconds == window_seconds).
